full_judgment: 3. Defendant No. 1 and 35-37 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the suit was barred by limitation and was bad for defect of parties and that the Dhaka Nawab Waqf Estate and Karatia Waqf Estate were the superior landlords, Gangadhar Namadas and his brothers were the tenants and they having defaulted in the payment of rent, their tenancy was sold in auction in a proceeding of 1933-1934 and the said tenancy was purchased by the Dhaka Nawab Waqf Estate. The land of the said tenancy along with other lands was settled to Momtazuddin, Abdul Quddus, Abdul Hakim, Intaz Ali and Abdul Hai. By amicable settlement Intaz Ali got land of plot Nos. 3146 and 3174 and he died leaving behind defendant No. 1 and three daughters (defendant Nos. 35-37) and defendant No. 1 by two deeds gave 91 decimals of land to his sisters. Defendant Nos. 1 and 35-37 were in possession of the suit land. The plaintiff has no right, title and interest in the suit plot Nos. 3146 and 3174 or in other words in the suit land.
